claims.text: The driver never placed an in-app call to the rider before cancelling. EV-TRIP-05063's own derived contact check records call_count 0, calls [] and obligation_met false, and the only in-app call anywhere in the trip record was placed_by the RIDER at 18:38:40. POL-NS-23 requires the driver to have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider, both before trip_record.cancelled_at, and where either is missing the fee is voided and the rider is not charged. The message limb is satisfied (driver messages MSG-05063-001 at 18:37:10 and MSG-05063-002 at 18:41:30, both before the 18:43:20 cancellation), but the call limb is not, so the 5.00 SGD fee must be voided, the rider is not charged, and no driver compensation follows.

The driver's disputed account that he 'called the passenger' is contradicted by the record. EV-TRIP-05063 shows exactly one in-app call for this trip, placed BY the rider at 18:38:40 and answered for 35 s, which is the very call the rider describes in her statement ('I called him to say I needed 5 more minutes'). POL-NS-23 requires the call to have been placed by the driver to the rider; a call the rider placed cannot discharge the driver's obligation, and the chat log (EV-CHAT-05063) contains two text messages only and no voice-call entry either.

The rider does not contest the wait, and the record is not stretched on it. This is an on-demand trip, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival; the auto-arrival is recorded at 18:36:50, the wait expired at 18:41:50, and the cancellation came at 18:43:20. That timing point is conceded. It does not save the fee, because POL-NS-23 imposes a separate contact condition on charging a no-show fee, and that condition failed on the call limb.

The 5.00 SGD has already been returned to the rider after her complaint: EV-FARE-05063 records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00 and total_charged 5.00, and EV-TRIP-05063 records the fee_reversed event at 2026-09-04T22:55:20 (refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver pending review). Because the DRIVER is the filing party and his claim fails on POL-NS-23, the present state stands and nothing moves back to him: the ruling should be NO_ACTION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both null, so the rider is not left carrying the disputed charge.

EV-ADVIS-05063-01 is MISSING: weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload. It carries no fact, and no no-show clause needs a traffic record — POL-NS-23's elements (the driver's messages, the driver's calls, and the cancellation time) are all carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0, as is the arrival time in EV-TRIP-05063. Its absence therefore raises no POL-GEN-26 open question about a fact this rule needs, and it cannot be used to withhold or escalate a case the record already settles.

The rider's no_show_cancellations_30d is 0, so POL-NS-25's repeat-no-show referral — which operates only at 3 or more, counting this trip if its fee stands — does not attach to her account, and no mandatory-upfront-payment or suspension referral arises. That field is the only profile field the policy permits to be cited for that rule, and it never changes the ruling on the trip.

claims.text: Trip TRP-05063 is an on-demand booking with no scheduled time, so POL-NS-21 runs the 300-second free wait from the driver's arrival: the driver arrived at 18:36:50 and cancelled at 18:43:20, 390 seconds later, 90 seconds beyond the free wait, so the no-show cancellation was validly made on the trip's own timings.

The 18:36:50 auto-arrival that starts the free wait is corroborated on the driver-device trace, whose nearest fix is 3.283 m from the pickup with a reported accuracy of 5 m, inside POL-NS-21's 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup, and whose intervals never exceed 30 s, so arrival rests on the GPS evidence and not on the trip record alone.

The payments ledger carries exactly one cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD and records the charge as matching the policy fee, so POL-NS-22 applies at its stated amount with no amount adjustment, and the driver is owed DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

POL-NS-23's message element is satisfied: the driver sent two in-app messages before cancelling (18:37:10, "Hi I'm downstairs at Blk 5", and 18:41:30, "Still waiting ah") and the chat log shows both were read by the rider (18:37:56 and 18:42:11), the second less than two minutes before the cancellation.

The no-show is admitted on the rider's own side: her counter-statement says she asked for five more minutes because she was finishing a work call, which places her away from the pickup when the free wait expired at 18:41:50, and the trip record's RIDER_NO_SHOW reason code is consistent with it; the driver waited the full period and the fee was earned on this trip's facts.

POL-NS-23's call element is the one element the driver cannot put up, and the driver states that plainly: in_app_calls carries a single 35-second answered call at 18:38:40 and the record attributes it to the rider, and the pre-pass derivation records call_count 0 and obligation_met false, so the driver does not assert a driver-placed call and does not ask the Tribunal to read the element away; the driver submits only that the parties were in live in-app voice contact during the free wait on the rider's own account, and that nothing else in the record displaces the fee earned under POL-NS-21 and POL-NS-22.

Every artifact the driver relies on is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so POL-GEN-02 sets no confidence ceiling on these facts, and at a contested value of 5.00 SGD POL-GEN-22 places the dispute below the 10.00 SGD band where POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final; the case should be decided on its merits rather than referred.

ruling.explanation:
Outcome: NO_ACTION. The 5.00 SGD no-show fee on trip TRP-05063 is void and stays refunded to the rider; nothing is returned to the driver.

The wait is common ground. This was an on-demand booking with no scheduled time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 18:36:50 (corroborated on the driver's GPS trace EV-GPS-05063, nearest fix 3.283 m from the pickup with 5 m reported accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, no interval over 30 s). The wait expired at 18:41:50 and the driver cancelled at 18:43:20, 390 s after arrival. The driver's timing claim (EV-TRIP-05063, EV-GPS-05063) is accepted.

But POL-NS-23 places a separate condition on charging a no-show fee: before cancelling, the driver must have sent at least one in-app message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider. EV-TRIP-05063's own contact check records call_count 0, calls [] and obligation_met false, and the only in-app call on this trip was placed BY the rider at 18:38:40 (the 35-second call the rider describes in her statement). The message limb is met (driver messages at 18:37:10 and 18:41:30, both read, both before the 18:43:20 cancellation), but the call limb is not: a call the rider placed cannot discharge the driver's obligation, and the driver's account that he 'called the passenger' is contradicted by the record. On POL-NS-23 the fee is therefore voided and the rider is not charged. The driver's DRIVER_COMPENSATION claim under POL-NS-22 is rejected: POL-NS-22 applies only where the fee stands, and it does not.

The 5.00 SGD is already back with the rider: EV-FARE-05063 records refund_issued_sgd 5.00, payment_status REFUNDED and total_charged 5.00, and EV-TRIP-05063 records the fee_reversed event at 2026-09-04T22:55:20. Because the driver is the filing party and the rider is owed that 5.00 SGD, the driver's claim fails and the present state stands under POL-GEN-03: NO_ACTION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both null.

No referral issues. POL-NS-25's repeat-no-show flag does not attach (the rider's counter is 0, and does not reach 3 counting this trip); POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not attach, since the driver did attempt contact by sending two in-app messages; and POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not fire, the fee charged having been exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee. The missing artifact EV-ADVIS-05063-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact and is needed by no no-show clause, so it raises no open question under POL-GEN-26.

Confidence: the deciding facts rest on complete, weight-1.0 artifacts (EV-TRIP-05063, EV-CHAT-05063, EV-GPS-05063, EV-FARE-05063), so POL-GEN-02(2) sets no ceiling below 1.0; at a contested value of 5.00 SGD this is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band and POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final, so the ruling issues at 0.95.

ruling.explanation:
This is the driver's filing against a refund the platform has already issued: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee was refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver (EV-FARE-05063: refund_issued_sgd 5.00, total_charged 5.00; EV-TRIP-05063: fee_reversed at 2026-09-04T22:55:20). The driver's claim to that 5.00 SGD fails, so nothing moves and the present state stands.

Why the fee does not stand: POL-NS-23 requires, before a driver cancels for no-show, BOTH (a) at least one in-app chat message from the driver to the rider, and (b) at least one in-app call placed BY the driver to the rider, each before the 18:43:20 cancellation. The message limb is met: MSG-05063-001 at 18:37:10 and MSG-05063-002 at 18:41:30 (EV-CHAT-05063), both read by the rider. The call limb is not met: EV-TRIP-05063 carries exactly one in-app call, placed_by the RIDER at 18:38:40 for 35 s, and its derived contact check records call_count 0, calls [] and obligation_met false; EV-CHAT-05063 contains two text messages and no voice-call entry. A call the rider placed cannot discharge the driver's obligation, so the driver's account that he 'called the passenger' is not supported by the record. Under POL-NS-23 one missing element voids the fee and the rider is not charged, with no driver compensation.

What is accepted on the driver's side: this is an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 18:36:50 and expired at 18:41:50; the cancellation at 18:43:20 came 390 s after arrival, 90 s beyond the wait. The arrival is corroborated by the GPS trace (nearest fix 3.283 m from the pickup, reported accuracy 5 m, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — EV-GPS-05063), and the ledger charged exactly the POL-NS-22 fee of 5.00 SGD. Those points are correct, but they do not decide the fee: POL-NS-23's contact condition is a separate gate, and it failed. The rider's concession that she asked for five more minutes is consistent with the timings and is treated as evidence, but it likewise does not cure the missing driver call.

To the rider: the 5.00 SGD stays with you, exactly as the platform already placed it, and you are not charged again.

To the driver: your claim to keep the fee is not supported; the 5.00 SGD already recovered from you is not returned, because the trip record shows you did not place the required in-app call before cancelling.

No referral attaches: the fee charged is the policy 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's amount check adds nothing; POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not arise (you did arrive and did message, so there was no failure to attempt contact); and the rider's no_show_cancellations_30d is 0, so POL-NS-25's repeat flag does not fire. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05063-01 (weight 0.0) carries no fact any no-show clause needs and raises no open question. The artifacts carrying the deciding facts (EV-TRIP-05063, EV-CHAT-05063, EV-FARE-05063) are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so no confidence ceiling applies, and at a contested value of 5.00 SGD below the 10.00 SGD band POL-NS-26 makes this ruling final.

To the driver: you filed to keep the 5.00 SGD no-show fee after the platform refunded it to the rider and recovered it from you. The timing is with you. This was an on-demand booking with no scheduled time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait ran from your arrival at the pickup at 18:36:50 (EV-TRIP-05063, corroborated by a GPS fix 3.28 m from the pickup at 5 m reported accuracy, EV-GPS-05063) and expired at 18:41:50; you cancelled at 18:43:20, 390 seconds after arriving, 90 seconds past the free wait. But POL-NS-23 puts a separate condition on charging a no-show fee: before cancelling you must have sent at least one in-app message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider, both before cancellation. You sent two messages (18:37:10 and 18:41:30, EV-CHAT-05063), so the message limb is met. The call limb is not. EV-TRIP-05063's in-app call record contains exactly one call, placed by the rider at 18:38:40 for 35 seconds; the record's own contact check records call_count 0 and obligation_met false, and EV-CHAT-05063 holds no voice-call entry either. A call the rider placed does not discharge your obligation, and your own submissions concede this limb cannot be put up. Under POL-NS-23 the 5.00 SGD fee is therefore voided and you receive no compensation. To the rider: the 5.00 SGD stays refunded to you. POL-NS-23 voids the fee, so you are not charged; EV-FARE-05063 already records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00 and total_charged 5.00, and the fee_reversed event at 2026-09-04T22:55:20 confirms the 5.00 SGD went back to you and was withheld from the driver. Because the driver is the filing party and his claim fails, POL-GEN-03 is read from the present state: NO_ACTION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both null. Nothing further is collected from you and nothing is returned to the driver. No referral attaches. The fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes, so the POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral does not arise; the driver did attempt contact, so POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not arise; and the rider profile's no_show_cancellations_30d is 0, below POL-NS-25's threshold of 3, so no repeat-no-show referral arises. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05063-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact any no-show clause needs, so it raises no POL-GEN-26 open question. Confidence rests on the COMPLETE weight-1.0 trip record and chat log that carry the deciding fact, and the contested value of 5.00 SGD is below 10.00 SGD, where POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 make the ruling final.

To both parties: the fee of 5.00 SGD does not stand, so nothing moves back to the driver and the money the rider has already received stays with her. Here is why.

The trip timings are not in dispute and the driver's account of them is correct. This was an on-demand booking, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait runs from arrival: the driver arrived at Block 5, Holland Close at 18:36:50 (recorded arrival corroborated by the driver-device trace EV-GPS-05063, whose nearest fix is 3.28 m from the pickup with a reported accuracy of 5 m, inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup), the free wait expired at 18:41:50, and the driver cancelled at 18:43:20 — 390 seconds after arrival, 90 seconds beyond the free wait (EV-TRIP-05063). The rider's own statement that she asked for five more minutes because she was finishing a work call confirms she was not at the pickup when the wait expired, and the RIDER_NO_SHOW reason code is consistent with that. The driver's free-wait and arrival points (POL-NS-21, EV-TRIP-05063, EV-GPS-05063) are therefore accepted.

Those points are not enough, because POL-NS-23 makes a no-show fee conditional on a separate contact obligation: before cancelling, the driver must have both sent at least one in-app message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider, both before cancelled_at. The message element is met — the driver messaged at 18:37:10 and 18:41:30 (EV-CHAT-05063, both read by the rider). The call element is not. The only in-app call on this trip is the one placed BY THE RIDER at 18:38:40 and answered for 35 seconds (EV-TRIP-05063, in_app_calls, placed_by RIDER); the trip record's own derived check records call_count 0 and obligation_met false, and the chat log (EV-CHAT-05063) contains two text messages and no voice-call entry. The driver's submission does not assert a driver-placed call — it concedes it cannot — and relies instead on the parties having been in live voice contact during the wait on the rider's account. That is correct as far as it goes, but POL-NS-23 requires the call to have been placed by the driver to the rider, and a call the rider placed does not discharge that obligation. So the driver's claims for DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD under POL-NS-22 are rejected, and the fee is voided under POL-NS-23: the rider is not charged, with no driver compensation.

On the money: EV-FARE-05063 records the 5.00 SGD fee as already refunded (payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00), and EV-TRIP-05063 records the fee_reversed event at 2026-09-04T22:55:20, refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver. The rider has therefore already received the 5.00 SGD she is owed. Because the driver is the filing party and his claim fails, the present state stands: the ruling is NO_ACTION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both null, so no further money moves and the disputed charge is not restored against the rider.

No referral attaches. POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag operates only at 3 or more no-shows counting this trip if the fee stands; the rider's rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is 0 and the fee does not stand, so it does not fire. POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not fire, because the ledger charged exactly the policy fee of 5.00 SGD. POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not fire either: the driver did arrive and did attempt contact, so the driver-no-show condition is absent. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05063-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact, and no no-show element this ruling needs — the driver's messages, the calls, the cancellation time and the arrival — depends on it, so its absence raises no POL-GEN-26 open question. All of the facts this ruling rests on come from COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-05063, EV-CHAT-05063), the contested value of 5.00 SGD sits below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and POL-NS-26 makes the ruling final at that value, so no escalation is warranted.
